## devonthink
CRITICAL — Database package safety: DEVONthink databases are stored as packages (.dtBase2) or sparse images (.dtSparse, .dtArchive). Never modify, rename, move, or delete files inside a database package directly via the filesystem. All record and content operations must go through this MCP server or, as a fallback, via AppleScript. Direct filesystem manipulation will corrupt the database and cause irreversible data loss.

Batch operations: Use the uuids array parameter instead of sequential single-record calls for tag, update, move, trash, duplicate, replicate, and export operations. Batch mode is faster, reduces round trips, and returns a summary with succeeded/failed counts.

Avoiding duplicates: Use lookup_records (by name, URL, path, filename, or comment) before create_record to check whether a record already exists.

Content editing: Prefer update_record_content with mode append or insert over replace for large documents. Replace mode requires sending the entire new content and risks accidental data loss if the content is incomplete.

Group hierarchies: Use create_group_path to create nested group structures in a single call (like mkdir -p) rather than sequential create_record calls.

AI-powered tools: classify_record and find_similar_records use DEVONthink's built-in AI algorithms and proprietary training data — they provide organizational suggestions that complement, not duplicate, your own capabilities.

Record enrichment: resolve_doi_metadata and resolve_book_metadata can enrich existing records with bibliographic metadata by passing the record's uuid — there is no need to create a new record.

AI exclusion: Records marked as excluded from AI access (excludeFromChat) are protected in two ways. (1) Input protection: any tool that receives such a record's UUID as an argument refuses to operate on it and returns an error. (2) Output protection: result lists from tools like search_records, classify_record, find_similar_records, get_record_children, get_record_duplicates, and the link traversal tools are filt… [truncated]

1	# Spending Report Design
2	
3	**Date:** 2026-07-09
4	**Status:** ✅ Built — table + chart views, cell drill-down, and hierarchy
5	editing (assign categories to groups, re-parent groups, add & rename Groupings)
6	are all shipped and live. Remaining work is the
7	[Deferred](#deferred-later-slices) slices (historical-year upload /
8	year-over-year, period selection, export). Grouping tier editing is now built;
9	what's left of "tier CRUD" is deliberately out of scope (fixed Importance areas,
10	no Grouping delete/reorder).
11	
12	## Overview
13	
14	A top-level **Spending** report that rolls up Expenses by **Importance →
15	Grouping → Category** across the months of a year. It replaces the Excel pivot
16	table the family currently maintains by hand. ("Spending Report" is the working
17	term; pin the final ubiquitous-language name in `domain-model.md` when built.)
18	
19	Built ✅: the **table view** (v1), the **chart view** (an accordion magnitude bar
20	chart), **cell drill-down** into the Expenses view, and **hierarchy editing**
21	(assign categories to groups, re-parent groups, assign-on-create) — see
22	[Implementation status](#implementation-status),
23	[Spending Chart](#spending-chart-graphical-presentation--built-),
24	[Drill-down](#drill-from-a-table-cell-into-the-expenses-view--built-), and
25	[Editable hierarchy](#editable-hierarchy--assign--re-parent--built-). Still
26	deferred: selectable periods, year-over-year comparison, historical-year upload,
27	tier CRUD, and export (see [Deferred](#deferred-later-slices)).
28	
29	## Data model (new)
30	
31	The category hierarchy today is flat: `categories (family_id, name, color)`.
32	There is no Grouping or Importance layer. v1 adds two tiers as real,
33	family-scoped tables so they are first-class and become editable later.
34	
35	- `importance_areas (id, family_id, name, sort_order)` — e.g. Essential
36	  (sort_order 1), Priorities (2), Other (3). The numeric prefix in the sample
37	  (`1. Essential`) becomes `sort_order`, not part of the name.
38	- `category_groups (id, family_id, name, importance_area_id)` — **Importance
39	  attaches to the Grouping**, not to individual categories. Matches the sample
40	  (all of Transportation is Essential) and makes the roll-up a clean two-hop
41	  join. If a future need arises for two categories in one group to have
42	  different importances, revisit — no counterexample in the current sample.
43	- `categories` gains `group_id → category_groups`. A Category belongs to a
44	  Group; the Group carries the Importance.
45	
46	**Seeding.** Derive default Importance areas and Groupings from
47	`docs/SampleHierachy.txt` (cleaned). Map the existing default categories into
48	Groups by name. Near-duplicate categories in the sample (`Car - Insurance` vs
49	`Car insurance`, `Gas` vs `Car - Gas`, `Parking` vs `Car - Parking`) are **not
50	auto-merged** — recognizable names are mapped, the rest fall to Uncategorized.
51	New families are seeded via the same path as `createDefaultCategories`, so any
52	future family gets a working report out of the box.
53	
54	## Report content
55	
56	- **Source:** receipts/Expenses (the app's source of truth for spending), **not**
57	  bank transactions. Bucketed by `transaction_date` (purchase date, not upload
58	  date).
59	- **Currency:** normalized to the family's display currency —
60	  `total_amount × (exchange_rate_to_cad ?? 1)`. CAD for now; the assumption is
61	  isolated so multi-currency drops in later.
62	- **Columns:** January → the last month that has any expense (left edge stays at
63	  January for a stable calendar grid). Interior/empty cells render blank, not
64	  `$0.00`. Final column is labelled **"Year to Date."**
65	- **Rows:** four row types — category detail, **Grouping subtotal**,
66	  **Importance subtotal**, and a final **Grand Total**. Importance ordered by
67	  `sort_order` (Essential → Priorities → Other); Groupings alphabetical within an
68	  Importance; Categories alphabetical within a Grouping. **Zero-activity rows are
69	  suppressed** (a category/group with no spend in the visible window is hidden).
70	- **Uncategorized:** rendered as its own section at the bottom, outside the real
71	  Importance/Grouping subtotals. It **is included in the Grand Total** (and any
72	  month-column totals), so the bottom-right number ties out to the family's
73	  actual total spend. The gap between the three Importance subtotals and the
74	  Grand Total is the deliberate nudge to go categorize.
75	- **Null amounts:** counted as `$0`. No new flag — the receipts and expenses
76	  pages already badge these (`⚠ Amount not read`). At most a small "N receipts
77	  missing an amount" footnote deep-linking to that existing filtered view.
78	
79	## Architecture
80	
81	- **Client-side pure aggregation.** A tested pure function
82	  `buildSpendingReport(expenses, hierarchy, year) → grid`, in the style of the
83	  CSV parsers and date utilities. The small hierarchy tables and the year's
84	  expenses are fetched separately and joined in TypeScript — the existing
85	  expense query is not widened. A family's yearly receipt count is small, so the
86	  data transfer is negligible and the logic stays unit-testable. If volume ever
87	  demands it, swap in a Postgres RPC behind the same function boundary — this
88	  avoids the RLS-fragility minefield the codebase repeatedly warns about.
89	- **Placement:** a new top-level **`/spending`** tab, following the existing
90	  `resolve()` / `filterQuery` nav pattern. May be promoted to the home page
91	  later once proven (currently `/` is "Family Receipts") — a separate change.
92	- **No editing UI in v1.** The hierarchy is hand-maintained (direct SQL) while
93	  the family is a single maintainer. The Uncategorized bucket is the feedback
94	  loop for anything unmapped.
95	
96	## Implementation status ✅
97	
98	v1 is built and running against live data (v0.50). What landed:
99	
100	- **Migration** `supabase/migrations/20260709_spending_hierarchy.sql` — creates
101	  `importance_areas` and `category_groups`, adds `categories.group_id`
102	  (`ON DELETE SET NULL`), family-scoped RLS mirroring `categories_family_access`,
103	  unique-per-family name indexes, and `updated_at` triggers. Ships
104	  `create_default_hierarchy(p_family_id)` (idempotent, `SECURITY DEFINER`): seeds
105	  3 Importance areas + 13 Groupings and maps categories → groups by name (a
106	  superset covering both the current default names and the older spreadsheet
107	  names). Backfills every existing family in a `DO` loop; the app calls it via
108	  RPC for new families.
109	- **Grouping → Importance seed choices.** Each Grouping is collapsed to a single
110	  Importance (the model attaches Importance to the Grouping): **Essential** =
111	  Everyday, Health, Home, Transportation, Income Taxes; **Priorities** = Banking
112	  & Investing, Debt, Fitness, Kids, Rental; **Other** = Discretionary, Gifts,
113	  Travel. Where the source spreadsheet split a Grouping across importances (e.g.
114	  Home's Garden/Household goods were "Other"), it now rolls up under the
115	  Grouping's single Importance. Change with a one-row `UPDATE` on
116	  `category_groups.importance_area_id`.
117	- **Aggregation** `src/lib/utils/spendingReport.ts` — the pure
118	  `buildSpendingReport(expenses, categories, groups, importanceAreas, year)`.
119	  21 unit tests in `spendingReport.spec.ts` (month columns, roll-up/subtotals,
120	  ordering, Uncategorized, refund netting, FX, null amounts, blank-vs-zero cells).
121	  Per-cell `{ amount, count }` drives blank (count 0) vs `0.00` (net-zero but had
122	  activity).
123	- **Types** `src/lib/types/Hierarchy.ts` (`ImportanceArea`, `CategoryGroup`);
124	  `Category` gains `group_id`.
125	- **Service** `CategoryService` gains `getFamilyImportanceAreas`,
126	  `getFamilyGroups`, and `createDefaultHierarchy` (RPC wrapper).
127	- **Page + nav** `src/routes/spending/+page.svelte` + a **Spending** top-level
128	  tab. Self-seeds the hierarchy on first open (mirrors default-categories
129	  lazy-init), then loads hierarchy + the year's expenses and paints the grid.
130	  Year prev/next selector, missing-amount footnote, Importance bands, Grouping
131	  and Importance subtotals, Uncategorized section, Grand Total.
132	- **Rendering details.** Long category names truncate to one line
133	  (`max-w-64 truncate`) with the full name on hover via `title`. The layout gives
134	  `/spending` full window width (`max-w-full`); other pages keep `max-w-5xl`.
135	
136	**Verification:** `npm run check`, `eslint`, and Prettier clean on touched files;
137	full unit suite green (1278 passed / 8 skipped, incl. the 21 new). Production
138	build succeeds. Not yet exercised: a rendered end-to-end pass (no local
139	auth/seed harness) — validated live by the maintainer instead.
140	
141	**Known open item surfaced by live data:** the seed maps by name, so any custom
142	or renamed category lands in Uncategorized until its `group_id` is set by hand.
143	
144	## Spending Chart (graphical presentation) — built ✅
145	
146	A `Table | Chart` toggle on `/spending` (shared year selector + loaded data)
147	adds a **magnitude bar chart** view (v0.60).
148	
149	> **Design note — why not stacked-by-month.** The first cut stacked 12 month
150	> segments per bar with a sequential ramp. In real data it failed twice: the 12
151	> subtle shades read as noise ("the gradient is a mess"), and one dominant
152	> Grouping (a family's ~$33k Home, driven by a one-off $20k renovation) crushed
153	> every other bar's height so small bars were unreadable. Both flaws trace to the
154	> month stack. v0.60 drops it: **solid magnitude bars + value labels**, with the
155	> month/time story deferred to the separate trend chart.
156	
157	- **Form:** one **solid bar per Grouping** = its year-to-date total, **coloured by
158	  Area of Importance** (a validated 3-colour categorical palette: Essential
159	  `#4f46e5`, Priorities `#0d9488`, Other `#d97706`; Uncategorized neutral gray).
160	  Bars ordered by Importance `sort_order` then Grouping name; **Uncategorized**
161	  trails; zero-activity groups suppressed.
162	- **Value label** above every bar (formatted currency), so a tiny bar next to a
163	  dominant one is still readable — the fix for the outlier problem without a
164	  scale hack. Positioned from the bound LayerChart `context` (band x-scale +
165	  linear y-scale).
166	- **Two bracket rows beneath the axis** carry the hierarchy, both positioned from
167	  the bound `context` band x-scale (aligned on resize):
168	  - **Row 1 — Grouping ± toggles.** One keyboard-focusable `<button>` bracket per
169	    Grouping, spanning its bar(s), showing `+ Name` / `− Name`. This is the
170	    expand/collapse control (see interaction) and the Grouping label.
171	  - **Row 2 — Area of Importance**, labelled **once per contiguous run** of
172	    same-Importance bars, in that Importance's colour. Uncategorized has no
173	    Importance bracket (its Grouping bracket names it).
174	- **Interaction: expand in place (accordion), not drill-and-replace.** Clicking a
175	  Grouping's bar **or** its ± bracket expands it into its **Category** bars _in
176	  place_ while its siblings stay visible; **any number of Groupings can be open at
177	  once** (`expandedGroups` is a reactive `SvelteSet`). Expanded Categories keep the
178	  parent Grouping's Importance colour and sit inside the same Importance bracket.
179	  Bars are keyed by a unique id, not name, so same-named Categories across
180	  Groupings don't collide on the band scale.
181	- **Click + hover come from a custom per-bar overlay, not LayerChart.** LayerChart's
182	  own tooltip layer both swallows bar clicks and can't carry a month breakdown, so
183	  `tooltipContext` is disabled and a transparent full-height column is drawn over
184	  each bar (from the band scale). It handles the click (toggle its Grouping) and the
185	  hover, which shows a **tooltip with the bar's name, its per-month totals, and the
186	  grand total** — the monthly detail dropped from the bars themselves. The overlay
187	  columns are `aria-hidden`/non-focusable mouse affordances; the ± brackets remain
188	  the keyboard-accessible controls.
189	- **Long labels don't collide.** When a Grouping expands into many Category bars,
190	  each axis label is truncated to one bar width with an ellipsis (`Meals and Drinks
191	Out` → `Meals…`); the full name is in the hover tooltip. Collapsed Grouping names
192	  live in their ± bracket (truncated there too). The one-line usage hint sits below
193	  the chart.
194	- **Data:** no new aggregation — the pure
195	  `buildSpendingChart(report, expandedGroups)` reshapes the existing
196	  `SpendingReport` into a flat `{ months, bars }` where expanded Groupings
197	  contribute their Category bars in place (unit-tested in `spendingChart.spec.ts`).
198	  The per-bar `monthly` map is retained for the future trend chart / hover detail;
199	  the current view uses only `total`.
200	- **Library:** **LayerChart 2.0.1** (`<BarChart>` with `y="total"` and a `c`
201	  ordinal colour scale by Importance; `bandPadding`, rounded bars). Peer
202	  `svelte@^5`. Its built-in tooltip/click layer (`tooltipContext`) is **disabled**
203	  in favour of the custom overlay above. Colours validated with the dataviz palette
204	  script (CVD ΔE 57.8, contrast ≥ 3:1); identity carried by position + brackets,
205	  not colour alone.
206	- **Verification:** `SpendingChart.svelte.spec.ts` (8 tests) renders it in Chromium
207	  and asserts: a bar per Grouping lays out, the once-only Importance brackets, the
208	  per-bar value labels, expand-in-place (siblings stay), several open at once,
209	  collapse back, **the bar itself (not just the bracket) expands**, and **the hover
210	  tooltip shows name + month totals + grand total**. `spendingChart.spec.ts`
211	  (6 tests) covers the pure accordion model; `spendingReport.spec.ts` (21) the
212	  aggregation.
213	
214	**Chart known limitation:**
215	
216	- **Prior-period overlay** (a line above/below the bar) is **not built** — it
217	  depends on historical-year data, which isn't loaded yet. Deferred with the
218	  upload/YoY thread below. Month-by-month detail currently lives in the Table
219	  view; a dedicated trend chart is the natural home for it.
220	
221	## Drill from a table cell into the Expenses view — built ✅
222	
223	The table's numbers are a jumping-off point (v0.55): clicking a non-blank cell
224	navigates to the **Expenses** view, filtered to exactly the Expenses that
225	produced that number.
226	
227	- **Category detail cell** (category × month) → that **category** in that
228	  **month**. **Category "Year to Date" cell** → that category across the year.
229	- **Subtotal cells** roll the filter up to match what they sum:
230	  - **Grouping subtotal** → every category id in that Grouping (that month/YTD).
231	  - **Importance subtotal** → every category id across the Importance's groups.
232	  - **Grand Total** → the date range alone (no category filter) so it ties out to
233	    all Expenses, **including Uncategorized**.
234	  - **Uncategorized** cells → the `filter=uncategorized` Expenses filter. A
235	    named-but-ungrouped category row instead drills to its own category id
236	    (precise); only the section subtotal and the "(No category)" row use the
237	    coarse `filter=uncategorized` (which by design covers only null-category
238	    Expenses, so a subtotal with ungrouped-category rows is a slight over-scope).
239	- **What shipped.**
240	  - **Pure** `buildSpendingDrilldownParams(scope, column, year, categories, groups)`
241	    → `URLSearchParams` in `src/lib/utils/spendingDrilldown.ts`; the scope
242	    (category / group / importance / uncategorized / grandTotal) and column
243	    (a month or YTD) come from the clicked row. 8 unit tests in

245	  - **Report identity.** `buildSpendingReport` rows/sections now carry the ids the

271	    Because Importance attaches to the Grouping, this re-buckets all the group's
272	    categories at once. `CategoryService.moveGroupToImportance(groupId, importanceAreaId)`.
273	- **Unassigned bucket up top.** Categories with no `group_id` render in an amber
274	  "Unassigned categories (N)" section — the editor's whole reason to exist — each
275	  with the same group picker. Below it, the full Importance → Grouping → Category
276	  tree with **zero-activity rows NOT suppressed** (unlike the report; every group
277	  and category must be assignable).
278	- **Architecture mirrors the report.** Pure `buildHierarchyTree(importanceAreas,
279	groups, categories) → { importances, unassigned }` in
280	  `src/lib/utils/hierarchyTree.ts` shapes the three flat tables into the nested
281	  tree (Importance by `sort_order`, Groupings/Categories alphabetical; orphan
282	  groups whose Importance FK doesn't resolve fold into a trailing synthetic node

324	appears.

330	- Arbitrary period / quarter selection (beyond a single calendar year).

# Spending Report Design

**Date:** 2026-07-09
**Status:** ✅ Built — table + chart views, cell drill-down, and hierarchy
editing (assign categories to groups, re-parent groups, add & rename Groupings)
are all shipped and live. Remaining work is the
[Deferred](#deferred-later-slices) slices (historical-year upload /
year-over-year, period selection, export). Grouping tier editing is now built;
what's left of "tier CRUD" is deliberately out of scope (fixed Importance areas,
no Grouping delete/reorder).

## Overview

A top-level **Spending** report that rolls up Expenses by **Importance →
Grouping → Category** across the months of a year. It replaces the Excel pivot
table the family currently maintains by hand. ("Spending Report" is the working
term; pin the final ubiquitous-language name in `domain-model.md` when built.)

Built ✅: the **table view** (v1), the **chart view** (an accordion magnitude bar
chart), **cell drill-down** into the Expenses view, and **hierarchy editing**
(assign categories to groups, re-parent groups, assign-on-create) — see
[Implementation status](#implementation-status),
[Spending Chart](#spending-chart-graphical-presentation--built-),
[Drill-down](#drill-from-a-table-cell-into-the-expenses-view--built-), and
[Editable hierarchy](#editable-hierarchy--assign--re-parent--built-). Still
deferred: selectable periods, year-over-year comparison, historical-year upload,
tier CRUD, and export (see [Deferred](#deferred-later-slices)).

## Data model (new)

The category hierarchy today is flat: `categories (family_id, name, color)`.
There is no Grouping or Importance layer. v1 adds two tiers as real,
family-scoped tables so they are first-class and become editable later.

- `importance_areas (id, family_id, name, sort_order)` — e.g. Essential
  (sort_order 1), Priorities (2), Other (3). The numeric prefix in the sample
  (`1. Essential`) becomes `sort_order`, not part of the name.
- `category_groups (id, family_id, name, importance_area_id)` — **Importance
  attaches to the Grouping**, not to individual categories. Matches the sample
  (all of Transportation is Essential) and makes the roll-up a clean two-hop
  join. If a future need arises for two categories in one group to have
  different importances, revisit — no counterexample in the current sample.
- `categories` gains `group_id → category_groups`. A Category belongs to a
  Group; the Group carries the Importance.

**Seeding.** Derive default Importance areas and Groupings from
`docs/SampleHierachy.txt` (cleaned). Map the existing default categories into
Groups by name. Near-duplicate categories in the sample (`Car - Insurance` vs
`Car insurance`, `Gas` vs `Car - Gas`, `Parking` vs `Car - Parking`) are **not
auto-merged** — recognizable names are mapped, the rest fall to Uncategorized.
New families are seeded via the same path as `createDefaultCategories`, so any
future family gets a working report out of the box.

## Report content

- **Source:** receipts/Expenses (the app's source of truth for spending), **not**
  bank transactions. Bucketed by `transaction_date` (purchase date, not upload
  date).
- **Currency:** normalized to the family's display currency —
  `total_amount × (exchange_rate_to_cad ?? 1)`. CAD for now; the assumption is
  isolated so multi-currency drops in later.
- **Columns:** January → the last month that has any expense (left edge stays at
  January for a stable calendar grid). Interior/empty cells render blank, not
  `$0.00`. Final column is labelled **"Year to Date."**
- **Rows:** four row types — category detail, **Grouping subtotal**,
  **Importance subtotal**, and a final **Grand Total**. Importance ordered by
  `sort_order` (Essential → Priorities → Other); Groupings alphabetical within an
  Importance; Categories alphabetical within a Grouping. **Zero-activity rows are
  suppressed** (a category/group with no spend in the visible window is hidden).
- **Uncategorized:** rendered as its own section at the bottom, outside the real
  Importance/Grouping subtotals. It **is included in the Grand Total** (and any
  month-column totals), so the bottom-right number ties out to the family's
  actual total spend. The gap between the three Importance subtotals and the
  Grand Total is the deliberate nudge to go categorize.
- **Null amounts:** counted as `$0`. No new flag — the receipts and expenses
  pages already badge these (`⚠ Amount not read`). At most a small "N receipts
  missing an amount" footnote deep-linking to that existing filtered view.

## Architecture

- **Client-side pure aggregation.** A tested pure function
  `buildSpendingReport(expenses, hierarchy, year) → grid`, in the style of the
  CSV parsers and date utilities. The small hierarchy tables and the year's
  expenses are fetched separately and joined in TypeScript — the existing
  expense query is not widened. A family's yearly receipt count is small, so the
  data transfer is negligible and the logic stays unit-testable. If volume ever
  demands it, swap in a Postgres RPC behind the same function boundary — this
  avoids the RLS-fragility minefield the codebase repeatedly warns about.
- **Placement:** a new top-level **`/spending`** tab, following the existing
  `resolve()` / `filterQuery` nav pattern. May be promoted to the home page
  later once proven (currently `/` is "Family Receipts") — a separate change.
- **No editing UI in v1.** The hierarchy is hand-maintained (direct SQL) while
  the family is a single maintainer. The Uncategorized bucket is the feedback
  loop for anything unmapped.

## Implementation status ✅

v1 is built and running against live data (v0.50). What landed:

- **Migration** `supabase/migrations/20260709_spending_hierarchy.sql` — creates
  `importance_areas` and `category_groups`, adds `categories.group_id`
  (`ON DELETE SET NULL`), family-scoped RLS mirroring `categories_family_access`,
  unique-per-family name indexes, and `updated_at` triggers. Ships
  `create_default_hierarchy(p_family_id)` (idempotent, `SECURITY DEFINER`): seeds
  3 Importance areas + 13 Groupings and maps categories → groups by name (a
  superset covering both the current default names and the older spreadsheet
  names). Backfills every existing family in a `DO` loop; the app calls it via
  RPC for new families.
- **Grouping → Importance seed choices.** Each Grouping is collapsed to a single
  Importance (the model attaches Importance to the Grouping): **Essential** =
  Everyday, Health, Home, Transportation, Income Taxes; **Priorities** = Banking
  & Investing, Debt, Fitness, Kids, Rental; **Other** = Discretionary, Gifts,
  Travel. Where the source spreadsheet split a Grouping across importances (e.g.
  Home's Garden/Household goods were "Other"), it now rolls up under the
  Grouping's single Importance. Change with a one-row `UPDATE` on
  `category_groups.importance_area_id`.
- **Aggregation** `src/lib/utils/spendingReport.ts` — the pure
  `buildSpendingReport(expenses, categories, groups, importanceAreas, year)`.
  21 unit tests in `spendingReport.spec.ts` (month columns, roll-up/subtotals,
  ordering, Uncategorized, refund netting, FX, null amounts, blank-vs-zero cells).
  Per-cell `{ amount, count }` drives blank (count 0) vs `0.00` (net-zero but had
  activity).
- **Types** `src/lib/types/Hierarchy.ts` (`ImportanceArea`, `CategoryGroup`);
  `Category` gains `group_id`.
- **Service** `CategoryService` gains `getFamilyImportanceAreas`,
  `getFamilyGroups`, and `createDefaultHierarchy` (RPC wrapper).
- **Page + nav** `src/routes/spending/+page.svelte` + a **Spending** top-level
  tab. Self-seeds the hierarchy on first open (mirrors default-categories
  lazy-init), then loads hierarchy + the year's expenses and paints the grid.
  Year prev/next selector, missing-amount footnote, Importance bands, Grouping
  and Importance subtotals, Uncategorized section, Grand Total.
- **Rendering details.** Long category names truncate to one line
  (`max-w-64 truncate`) with the full name on hover via `title`. The layout gives
  `/spending` full window width (`max-w-full`); other pages keep `max-w-5xl`.

**Verification:** `npm run check`, `eslint`, and Prettier clean on touched files;
full unit suite green (1278 passed / 8 skipped, incl. the 21 new). Production
build succeeds. Not yet exercised: a rendered end-to-end pass (no local
auth/seed harness) — validated live by the maintainer instead.

**Known open item surfaced by live data:** the seed maps by name, so any custom
or renamed category lands in Uncategorized until its `group_id` is set by hand.

## Spending Chart (graphical presentation) — built ✅

A `Table | Chart` toggle on `/spending` (shared year selector + loaded data)
adds a **magnitude bar chart** view (v0.60).

> **Design note — why not stacked-by-month.** The first cut stacked 12 month
> segments per bar with a sequential ramp. In real data it failed twice: the 12
> subtle shades read as noise ("the gradient is a mess"), and one dominant
> Grouping (a family's ~$33k Home, driven by a one-off $20k renovation) crushed
> every other bar's height so small bars were unreadable. Both flaws trace to the
> month stack. v0.60 drops it: **solid magnitude bars + value labels**, with the
> month/time story deferred to the separate trend chart.

- **Form:** one **solid bar per Grouping** = its year-to-date total, **coloured by
  Area of Importance** (a validated 3-colour categorical palette: Essential
  `#4f46e5`, Priorities `#0d9488`, Other `#d97706`; Uncategorized neutral gray).
  Bars ordered by Importance `sort_order` then Grouping name; **Uncategorized**
  trails; zero-activity groups suppressed.
- **Value label** above every bar (formatted currency), so a tiny bar next to a
  dominant one is still readable — the fix for the outlier problem without a
  scale hack. Positioned from the bound LayerChart `context` (band x-scale +
  linear y-scale).
- **Two bracket rows beneath the axis** carry the hierarchy, both positioned from
  the bound `context` band x-scale (aligned on resize):
  - **Row 1 — Grouping ± toggles.** One keyboard-focusable `<button>` bracket per
    Grouping, spanning its bar(s), showing `+ Name` / `− Name`. This is the
    expand/collapse control (see interaction) and the Grouping label.
  - **Row 2 — Area of Importance**, labelled **once per contiguous run** of
    same-Importance bars, in that Importance's colour. Uncategorized has no
    Importance bracket (its Grouping bracket names it).
- **Interaction: expand in place (accordion), not drill-and-replace.** Clicking a
  Grouping's bar **or** its ± bracket expands it into its **Category** bars _in
  place_ while its siblings stay visible; **any number of Groupings can be open at
  once** (`expandedGroups` is a reactive `SvelteSet`). Expanded Categories keep the
  parent Grouping's Importance colour and sit inside the same Importance bracket.
  Bars are keyed by a unique id, not name, so same-named Categories across
  Groupings don't collide on the band scale.
- **Click + hover come from a custom per-bar overlay, not LayerChart.** LayerChart's
  own tooltip layer both swallows bar clicks and can't carry a month breakdown, so
  `tooltipContext` is disabled and a transparent full-height column is drawn over
  each bar (from the band scale). It handles the click (toggle its Grouping) and the
  hover, which shows a **tooltip with the bar's name, its per-month totals, and the
  grand total** — the monthly detail dropped from the bars themselves. The overlay
  columns are `aria-hidden`/non-focusable mouse affordances; the ± brackets remain
  the keyboard-accessible controls.
- **Long labels don't collide.** When a Grouping expands into many Category bars,
  each axis label is truncated to one bar width with an ellipsis (`Meals and Drinks
Out` → `Meals…`); the full name is in the hover tooltip. Collapsed Grouping names
  live in their ± bracket (truncated there too). The one-line usage hint sits below
  the chart.
- **Data:** no new aggregation — the pure
  `buildSpendingChart(report, expandedGroups)` reshapes the existing
  `SpendingReport` into a flat `{ months, bars }` where expanded Groupings
  contribute their Category bars in place (unit-tested in `spendingChart.spec.ts`).
  The per-bar `monthly` map is retained for the future trend chart / hover detail;
  the current view uses only `total`.
- **Library:** **LayerChart 2.0.1** (`<BarChart>` with `y="total"` and a `c`
  ordinal colour scale by Importance; `bandPadding`, rounded bars). Peer
  `svelte@^5`. Its built-in tooltip/click layer (`tooltipContext`) is **disabled**
  in favour of the custom overlay above. Colours validated with the dataviz palette
  script (CVD ΔE 57.8, contrast ≥ 3:1); identity carried by position + brackets,
  not colour alone.
- **Verification:** `SpendingChart.svelte.spec.ts` (8 tests) renders it in Chromium
  and asserts: a bar per Grouping lays out, the once-only Importance brackets, the
  per-bar value labels, expand-in-place (siblings stay), several open at once,
  collapse back, **the bar itself (not just the bracket) expands**, and **the hover
  tooltip shows name + month totals + grand total**. `spendingChart.spec.ts`
  (6 tests) covers the pure accordion model; `spendingReport.spec.ts` (21) the
  aggregation.

**Chart known limitation:**

- **Prior-period overlay** (a line above/below the bar) is **not built** — it
  depends on historical-year data, which isn't loaded yet. Deferred with the
  upload/YoY thread below. Month-by-month detail currently lives in the Table
  view; a dedicated trend chart is the natural home for it.

## Drill from a table cell into the Expenses view — built ✅

The table's numbers are a jumping-off point (v0.55): clicking a non-blank cell
navigates to the **Expenses** view, filtered to exactly the Expenses that
produced that number.

- **Category detail cell** (category × month) → that **category** in that
  **month**. **Category "Year to Date" cell** → that category across the year.
- **Subtotal cells** roll the filter up to match what they sum:
  - **Grouping subtotal** → every category id in that Grouping (that month/YTD).
  - **Importance subtotal** → every category id across the Importance's groups.
  - **Grand Total** → the date range alone (no category filter) so it ties out to
    all Expenses, **including Uncategorized**.
  - **Uncategorized** cells → the `filter=uncategorized` Expenses filter. A
    named-but-ungrouped category row instead drills to its own category id

    coarse `filter=uncategorized` (which by design covers only null-category

- **What shipped.**
  - **Pure** `buildSpendingDrilldownParams(scope, column, year, categories, groups)`

    `spendingDrilldown.spec.ts`.
  - **Report identity.** `buildSpendingReport` rows/sections now carry the ids the
    drill-down needs: `ReportRow.categoryId`, `GroupSection.id`,
    `ImportanceSection.id` (additive; 6 new tests, 27 total in
    `spendingReport.spec.ts`).
  - **Page.** `/spending` table cells render as `<a href>` links to `/expenses?…`;
    **blank cells (count 0) are not links**.
- **Real Expenses-page contract** (corrects the earlier guess): the params are
  **`dateFrom`/`dateTo`** (inclusive `YYYY-MM-DD`, via `readDateFilter`), category
  is **`category=id,id`**, and uncategorized is **`filter=uncategorized`** — which
  takes precedence over `category`, so the two are never set together.
- **Not yet:** the same affordance on chart bars (deferred). Verified live by the
  maintainer (no auth/seed harness for an end-to-end render pass), like v1.

## Editable hierarchy — assign & re-parent — built ✅

An **Edit hierarchy** page at **`/spending/hierarchy`** (linked from a button on
`/spending`) lets the maintainer restructure the hierarchy without SQL (v0.65).
This directly closes the "Known open item" above: custom/renamed categories that
the name-based seed left in Uncategorized can now be pulled into a Grouping in
the UI.

- **Two mutations shipped** (the highest-value slice):
  - **Assign a Category to a Grouping** (or back to Uncategorized) — a per-category
    `<select>` grouped by Importance via `<optgroup>`.
    `CategoryService.assignCategoryToGroup(categoryId, groupId | null)`.
  - **Move a Grouping to another Area of Importance** — a per-group `<select>`.
    Because Importance attaches to the Grouping, this re-buckets all the group's
    categories at once. `CategoryService.moveGroupToImportance(groupId, importanceAreaId)`.
- **Unassigned bucket up top.** Categories with no `group_id` render in an amber

  with the same group picker. Below it, the full Importance → Grouping → Category
  tree with **zero-activity rows NOT suppressed** (unlike the report; every group
  and category must be assignable).
- **Architecture mirrors the report.** Pure `buildHierarchyTree(importanceAreas,
groups, categories) → { importances, unassigned }` in
  `src/lib/utils/hierarchyTree.ts` shapes the three flat tables into the nested
  tree (Importance by `sort_order`, Groupings/Categories alphabetical; orphan
  groups whose Importance FK doesn't resolve fold into a trailing synthetic node
  so nothing is silently dropped). Presentation is a pure
  `HierarchyEditor.svelte` (props in, `onAssignCategory`/`onMoveGroup` out); the
  page owns loading + the CategoryService calls and reloads after each mutation.
  The page self-seeds the hierarchy if empty, like `/spending`.
- **Verification.** `hierarchyTree.spec.ts` (8, pure tree) +
  `HierarchyEditor.svelte.spec.ts` (5, renders the bucket/sections and asserts the
  selects emit the right ids incl. assign-to-null). `check`/eslint/Prettier clean;
  full suite green; production build succeeds. Live end-to-end pass by the
  maintainer (no auth/seed harness), like the earlier slices.

- **Assign-on-create (v0.66).** The inline "Create new category…" form in
  `CategoryDropdown` (expenses page) now offers an optional **Group** selector, so
  a category can be filed into a Grouping at birth instead of landing in
  Uncategorized. `CategoryService.createCategory` gained an optional 4th `groupId`
  arg; the expenses page loads the family's Groupings and passes them in. The
  selector is hidden when no Groupings are supplied, so the receipt/reconciliation
  uses of `CategoryDropdown` (which don't pass `groups`) are unchanged. Tests: 3

- **Add & rename Groupings (v0.67).** The editor now creates new Groupings and
  renames existing ones, so the tier is no longer SQL-only. An **"Add a Grouping"**
  form (name + Area of Importance) sits below the tree
  (`CategoryService.createGroup(familyId, name, importanceAreaId)`); the new empty
  group appears in its area, ready to have categories assigned into it. Each
  Grouping header has an inline **Rename** (`CategoryService.renameGroup(groupId,
name)`) — safe because the report and editor key off the group id, not its name.
  Both service methods validate the name and map the unique-per-family `23505`
  violation to a friendly message. Tests: 4 new in `CategoryService.spec.ts`
  (create + rename, validation, duplicate-name), 3 in
  `HierarchyEditor.svelte.spec.ts` (add emits name+area, add stays disabled until
  both set, rename emits the edited name).

**Out of scope — the Importance tier is fixed, permanently.** The 3 seeded areas
(Essential / Priorities / Other) will **not** change: there is no add/rename/
reorder UI and none is planned — this is a settled product decision, not a
deferral. Treat Importance-area CRUD as a non-goal.

**Still deferred (Groupings):** Groupings have **no delete** — an empty Grouping
is inert since the report suppresses zero-activity rows, so deleting it (and the
delete-confirmation it would need) buys nothing. Grouping `sort_order` reorder is
also unbuilt (Groupings render alphabetically). Revisit only if a real need
appears.

## Deferred (later slices)

- Prior-period overlay line + year-over-year comparison (needs historical data).
- Historical-year expense upload (unblocks the two above).
- Arbitrary period / quarter selection (beyond a single calendar year).
- The multi-chart-type menu and any second chart type (trend, magnitude).
- Hierarchy tier CRUD — mostly built (assign + re-parent, and now **add/rename
  Groupings**, v0.67). **Importance-area CRUD is a permanent non-goal** — the 3
  seeded areas are fixed and will not change. Not built (but possible later):
  **Grouping delete** (empty groups are inert) and **Grouping reorder**
  (`sort_order`). See the Editable-hierarchy section above.
- Export (CSV / PDF).
- Promoting the report to the home page.

## Known limitations (document when building)

- **Refunds.** Refunds are represented as **negative `total_amount`** on a
  receipt (confirmed via `formatCurrency.spec.ts` and the export services). The
  report **keeps the sign**, so refunds net against spend — which is the correct
  behaviour for a spending total. (Note the CSV/PDF _exporters_ deliberately
  `abs()` refunds; the report does not.) One visible consequence: a Category or
  Grouping whose refunds exceed its spend in the window shows a **negative**
  total — informative, not a bug. No special handling needed in v1; documented
  here so the divergence from the exporters is intentional and searchable.
- **"Year to Date" label** reads oddly for a _completed past_ year (it is the
  full-year total). Relabel per-context when the multi-year slice lands. Not a
  v1 problem since v1 is current-year only.

Resolved by routing each concern to its real owner: date-filter URL parse/generate/filter were **redundant** with `sharedDateFilter.spec.ts` (49 real tests) → deleted; the genuine `getValidDate` tests (its only coverage) **moved** to `dateValidation.spec.ts`; the uncategorized and category filters became **render tests** on the expenses page (`expenses-page.svelte.spec.ts` — toggle the Uncategorized button / pick a category, assert the visible rows + filtered count, both teeth-proven); sorting is owned by `DataTable.svelte.spec.ts`; the spending-summary reimplementation guarded **unbuilt UI** (no summary panel is rendered) → deleted. Both teeth-proven. **Third offender (later found):** `ReceiptImageViewer.spec.ts` (859 lines) was the worst of the lot — every `it()` re-declared the zoom arithmetic _inline_ (`let zoom = 100; zoom += 50; expect(zoom).toBe(150)`) and asserted against its own copy, never rendering the component (its header admitted it was stale TDD RED-phase scaffolding). 61:- **Remove/implement unimplemented & placeholder tests. ✅ DONE (main finds).** (a) `CategoryService.spec.ts` was stale TDD **RED-phase scaffolding** — a dynamic `import()` in try/catch with a dead `if (!CategoryService) { expect.fail('not implemented yet'); return; }` guard in all 28 tests, even though the service has long existed. Stripped the scaffolding → static typed import; also replaced the whole `any`-typed mock with a typed `MockQueryBuilder` (24 `any`s → 0). 28 tests unchanged. (b) `CSVExportService.spec.ts`'s two empty `it.skip('… browser only')` placeholders → **implemented for real** in `CSVExportService.svelte.spec.ts` (client project): asserts the anchor download fires and — via raw-bytes (`EF BB BF`, since `Blob.text()` strips a leading BOM) — that the UTF-8 BOM is present for Excel. Teeth-proven. Non-finds: `ReceiptService.bulk.spec.ts`'s `expect.fail` are legit "should have thrown" guards. `family-category-visibility.spec.ts` — **decision made: KEEP.** It's an env-gated (`describeIf(SUPABASE_URL && SERVICE_KEY)`) RLS integration suite — never runs in CI, but it's the _only_ executable check of the family-scoping row-level-security policies the migrations define (removed members can't see data, unique constraints), which unit tests can't cover. Fixed a real bug (it re-evaluated `Date.now()` for the sign-in emails, so they never matched the `createUser` emails → every sign-in would fail); emails are now computed once per run, and the header documents how to run it against `supabase start`. A handful of hollow `expect(typeof service.X).toBe('function')` "has-method" checks remain, scattered one-per-suite — low value, not removed.

66:- **Extract a shared fetch-mock fixture. ✅ DONE (2026-07-09).** `src/lib/tests/fixtures/fetchMock.ts` exports `stubFetchJson(body, {ok,status})` / `stubFetchReject(error)` / `installFetchMock()` (save→restore, for `beforeEach`/`afterEach`), centralising the `{ ok, json }` Response shape and the `as unknown as typeof fetch` cast. Full unit suite green (1240), `svelte-check` 0/0.

content.text:
The design doc is thorough and the current status is clear: **table view, chart view, cell drill-down, and hierarchy editing are all shipped and live (v0.67).** Everything remaining is in the [Deferred](#deferred-later-slices) list. Here's what's actually left and how I'd sequence it:

## Remaining work, grouped by dependency

**The big thread — needs historical data (do these in order):**
1. **Historical-year expense upload** — the keystone. Nothing in the year-over-year story can be built until multiple years of expenses exist. This unblocks the next two.

<result>I have everything needed. Here is the complete picture of how a single expense is created today and what a CSV row must supply.

## 1. `receipts` table schema

Base table `supabase/migrations/001_init.sql:5-17`, extended by later migrations. Full column list:

| Column | Type | Nullable | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | uuid PK | no | `default gen_random_uuid()` |
| `user_id` | uuid | no | FK `auth.users`, cascade. **Auto-set by trigger** if null (`001_init.sql:36-47`) |
| `family_id` | uuid | yes | FK `families`, `ON DELETE SET NULL`. Added `20251010000319_remote_schema.sql:113`; **auto-set by `set_receipt_family_id` trigger** (`:383`) to the user's default active family |
| `receipt_image_path` | text | **yes (nullable)** | `001_init.sql:8` — **a receipt can exist with NO image** (this is how manual receipts work) |
| `transaction_date` | `date` | yes | `001_init.sql:9`. Stored as `YYYY-MM-DD` (see model `src/lib/models/Receipt.ts:5`) |
| `total_amount` | numeric | yes | `001_init.sql:10` |
| `tax` | numeric | yes | `001_init.sql:11` |
| `merchant_name` | text | yes | `001_init.sql:12` |
| `credit_card_name` | text | yes | `001_init.sql:13` |
| `credit_card_last_4` | text | yes | `001_init.sql:14` |
| `currency` | text | yes | `001_init.sql:15` |
| `exchange_rate_to_cad` | `numeric(10,6)` | yes | default NULL. `20260405_add_exchange_rate_to_receipts.sql:4` |
| `matched_transaction_id` | uuid | yes | reconciliation link |
| `suspicious_date` | boolean | **no** | `DEFAULT FALSE NOT NULL`. `011_add_suspicious_date_flag.sql:13` — flag for dates >42 days old or future |
| `split_group_id` | uuid | yes | `20260228_receipt_split_groups.sql` |
| `original_filename` | text | yes | `20260607_add_original_filename_to_receipts.sql:4` |
| `created_at` | timestamptz | no | `default now()` |

TypeScript mirror: `ReceiptRow` / `ReceiptInsert` in `src/lib/models/Receipt.ts:1-18` and `:132-146`. Note: the model omits `family_id`; `ReceiptService` re-adds it locally as `InsertedReceiptRow` (`src/lib/services/ReceiptService.ts:17`).

RLS: insert requires `auth.uid() = user_id` (`001_init.sql:25-27`); reads allow family members (`20251010000319_remote_schema.sql`).

## 2. `expense_categories` table — receipt↔category link

`supabase/migrations/010_expense_categorization.sql:40-46`. **Strictly 1:1** — `receipt_id` is the PRIMARY KEY:
- `receipt_id` uuid **PK**, FK `receipts(id)` ON DELETE CASCADE
- `category_id` uuid, FK `categories(id)` ON DELETE SET NULL (nullable)
- `categorization_source` varchar(10) **NOT NULL**, CHECK IN `('manual','auto')`
- `created_at`, `updated_at` timestamptz

A receipt has at most one category row; upserting on `receipt_id` conflict is how re-categorization works.

## 3. `categories` table schema

Created `010_expense_categorization.sql:19-26` (originally user-scoped), then migrated to family scope:
- `id` uuid PK
- `family_id` uuid **NOT NULL**, FK `families` cascade (`20260111000001_migrate_categories_to_family_scope.sql:18,80`)
- `name` varchar(100) NOT NULL
- `color` varchar(7) nullable (hex `#RRGGBB`)
- `group_id` uuid nullable, FK `category_groups` ON DELETE SET NULL — NULL = "Uncategorized" in spending report (`20260709_spending_hierarchy.sql:61`)
- `created_at`, `updated_at`
- **UNIQUE `(family_id, LOWER(name))`** — case-insensitive per family (`:95-96`). Violations return Postgres code `23505`.

## 4. `ReceiptService` — creation paths

Two creation methods, `src/lib/services/ReceiptService.ts`:

**`uploadAndCreate(file)` (`:186-199`)** — the image path. REQUIRES a `File`: validates it (`:164-177`), resizes, uploads to the `receipts` storage bucket (`uploadToStorage` `:222-236`, path = `${user.id}/${uuid}.${ext}`), runs OCR best-effort, then inserts. Not usable for CSV.

**`createManual(values)` (`:142-162`)** — **the image-free path you want.** Signature requires `merchant_name`, `total_amount`, `transaction_date` (plus any optional `ReceiptInsert` fields), does a plain `insert` with `suspicious_date: false` forced (skips date validation for intentional old entries), no storage upload, no `receipt_image_path`. `user_id` and `family_id` are filled by DB triggers, so the client need not send them (though RLS requires the caller be authenticated and the row's `user_id` = `auth.uid()`).

Neither method sets a category — categorization is a separate step (§5).

## 5. Category resolve / find-or-create

`CategoryService` (`src/lib/services/CategoryService.ts`) has **no `getByName`/find-or-create helper**. The pieces:
- `getFamilyCategories(familyId)` (`:129-148`) — returns all categories for a family, ordered by name. The app loads this list once and resolves names/ids client-side.
- `createCategory(familyId, name, color?, groupId?)` (`:407-455`) — inserts; on duplicate (`23505`) throws "A category with this name already exists". So find-or-create = search the loaded list case-insensitively, else `createCategory`.
- Client-side resolution helpers: `src/lib/utils/resolveCategory.ts` — `findCategoryById` (`:50-52`) and `resolveCategory` (`:28-41`). There is **no name-based lookup util**; you must match `name` yourself (the DB unique index is on `LOWER(name)`).

**Assigning the category to a receipt** is done by `ExpenseService.assignCategory(receiptId, categoryId, source='manual')` (`src/lib/services/ExpenseService.ts:213-243`) — upserts into `expense_categories` on conflict `receipt_id`. There's also `bulkAssignCategory(receiptIds[], categoryId, source)` (`:255-284`) which batch-upserts many receipts to one category in a single call.

`family_id` for the current user comes from `getDefaultFamilyId()` in `src/lib/utils/familyUtils.ts:14-32` (highest `is_default`, active membership).

## 6. `transaction_date` storage & date utils

Postgres `date` column; carried as `string | null` in `YYYY-MM-DD` form (`src/lib/models/Receipt.ts:5`). Utilities in `src/lib/utils/dateConversion.ts`:
- `toDate(isoString)` (`:7-16`) — parses `YYYY-MM-DD` into a local `Date` (manual split to avoid TZ shift); returns `undefined` on empty/invalid.
- `toISODateString(date)` (`:48-54`) — formats a `Date` back to `YYYY-MM-DD` using local getters; `''` on null/invalid.
- `formatDate` (`:22-30`) display-only.

Manual-receipt validation lives in `src/lib/utils/manualReceipt.ts`: `validateManualReceipt` (`:34-53`) requires non-empty `merchant_name` and `total_amount > 0`; `transaction_date` is passed through as-is (defaulted to today by `newManualReceiptForm`). Note it does **not** itself validate the date string format — the receipts page relies on the picker.

## 7. Existing bulk paths

- **No bulk receipt-create exists.** `ReceiptService.bulk.spec.ts` and the service only implement `bulkDeleteReceipts(ids[])` (`ReceiptService.ts:609-628`) — a single `delete().in('id', ids).eq('user_id', ...)`.
- For categorization there IS a batch path: `ExpenseService.bulkAssignCategory` (`ExpenseService.ts:255-284`).
- To bulk-create receipts you would replicate the `createManual` pattern with a single `.from('receipts').insert([...rows])` array insert (the triggers still fire per row for `user_id`/`family_id`).

---

## Summary: what a CSV row needs to become a valid expense

A valid expense = one `receipts` row + one `expense_categories` row pointing at a `categories` row (all sharing the user's `family_id`).

**Per CSV row, minimum to create the receipt** (via `createManual`-style insert):
- `merchant_name` (required by validation/app; column is nullable but the UI enforces it)
- `total_amount` > 0 (required by validation; column nullable)
- `transaction_date` as `YYYY-MM-DD` (nullable, but you'll want it)
- `receipt_image_path` — **omit/null; fully supported, no image required**
- `suspicious_date` — set to `false` (createManual forces this)
- Optional: `tax`, `currency`, `exchange_rate_to_cad`, `credit_card_name`, `credit_card_last_4`, `original_filename`
- **Do NOT send** `user_id` / `family_id` — DB triggers set them from `auth.uid()` / default family. Caller must be authenticated (RLS).

**Then, to make it a categorized expense:**
1. Resolve category name → id against `getFamilyCategories(familyId)` (case-insensitive match on `LOWER(name)`); create missing ones with `createCategory(familyId, name)` (handle `23505` = already exists).
2. Insert `expense_categories` row: `{ receipt_id, category_id, categorization_source: 'manual' }` — via `assignCategory` (one) or `bulkAssignCategory` (many), or a direct batch upsert on `receipt_id`.

Key gotcha: receipt insert must return `id` before you can write `expense_categories` (FK + PK on `receipt_id`), so a bulk flow is: batch-insert receipts with `.select()`, then batch-upsert `expense_categories` using the returned ids.</result>

content.text:
I now have the full picture. Good news: **no schema change or migration is needed** — the pieces already exist.

## What makes this clean

- **Imageless receipts already work.** `ReceiptService.createManual()` inserts a `receipts` row with `receipt_image_path` null, `suspicious_date` forced `false`, and DB triggers fill `user_id`/`family_id`. That's exactly a historical expense.
- **Sign convention already matches.** Your CSV uses *positive = expense, negative = refund* (e.g. `Mark's -21.18`, `Sporting Life -394.35` are returns). The `receipts.total_amount` column uses the same convention, and the spending report already keeps the sign so refunds net against spend. **No inversion, no `abs()`.**
- **Category names mostly already exist.** Values like `Coffee and Tea`, `Sports and Fitness`, `Car - Other Expenses`, `Groceries` match the app's default category names, so `getFamilyCategories()` will resolve most by name; only genuinely new ones get created.
- **Reusable parsing/dedup.** `convertExcelToCSV` + `FileReader`, the hand-rolled CSV tokenizer, `parseDate`/`parseAmount`, and the count-based `computeImportPlan` dedup pattern are all reusable.

## Proposed design (mirrors the existing pure-core/imperative-shell style)

1. **Pure parser** `src/lib/utils/expenseImportCsv.ts` — `parseExpenseImportCsv(csvText) → { rows, errors }`, each row `{ transaction_date, merchant_name, total_amount, categoryName }`. Unit-tested. Reuses the existing tokenizer + date/amount helpers.
2. **Pure plan** `src/lib/utils/expenseImportPlan.ts` — given parsed rows + existing receipts-in-range + existing categories → `{ toInsert, duplicatesSkipped, newCategoryNames }`. Count-based dedup keyed `date|merchant|amount|category` so re-importing the same file is safe. Unit-tested.
3. **Service** `ExpenseImportService.importFromCsv(familyId, file)` — reads file, runs the pure parser + plan, creates missing categories, batch-inserts receipts with `.select()` to get ids, then batch-upserts `expense_categories` (`source: 'manual'`). Returns a summary.
4. **Route** `/expenses/import` — upload UI + a **preview/confirm** step (rows to import, new categories to be created, duplicates to skip), then commit. Reached by a button on `/expenses` and `/spending`.

## Three decisions before I build

1. **The `Tag` column has nowhere to land** — there's no tag concept anywhere in the schema (no column, no table). My recommendation: **ignore `Tag` in v1** (parse-and-drop). What's actually in that column, and do you need it preserved? If yes, it's a small migration (`receipts.tag`) — say the word.

	// Shared inline success/error banner for the list pages (RF-03 follow-up).
	// One placement (top of page, full width) and one look everywhere, replacing
	// the per-page mix of plain banners, icon banners and a fixed corner toast.

	let {

		message,
		onDismiss
	}: {
		type?: 'success' | 'error';
		message: string;
		onDismiss?: () => void;
	} = $props();

	const containerClass = $derived(
		type === 'error'
			? 'border-red-200 bg-red-50 text-red-800'
			: 'border-green-200 bg-green-50 text-green-800'
	);

	// Heroicons: check-circle for success, exclamation-circle for error.

	);

input.new_string:
## Historical-year expense upload — built ✅

A **Import Expenses** page at **`/expenses/import`** (buttons on both `/expenses`
and `/spending`) imports historical Expenses from a CSV / XLS / XLSX file
(v0.70). This is the keystone of the year-over-year thread: it's the only way to
get prior years' Expenses into the app so the deferred prior-period overlay /
YoY slices have data to compare against.

- **File format.** Columns `Timestamp, Merchant, Amount, Category` (a `Tag`
  column is parsed-and-dropped — there is no tag concept in the schema). `Amount`
  keeps its sign: **positive = expense, negative = refund**, the same convention
  as `receipts.total_amount`, so refunds net against spend exactly as real
  receipts do (no inversion, no `abs()`). `Category` is a plain name; blank →
  Uncategorized.
- **Each row becomes an imageless receipt + a category link.** No schema change
  was needed: `receipts.receipt_image_path` is nullable and `createManual`
  already creates receipts with no image and `suspicious_date` forced `false`
  (these are intentional old entries). A row is one `receipts` insert plus, when
  it has a category, one `expense_categories` upsert (`source: 'manual'`).
  Category names resolve against the family's categories case-insensitively;
  genuinely new names are **created** and land in Uncategorized until filed in
  the hierarchy editor.
- **Two-step preview → confirm.** Unlike the transaction importer (which commits
  straight to the DB), this shows a preview first: how many expenses will import,
  how many duplicates will be skipped, which new categories will be created (with
  a warning + link to the hierarchy editor), and any unreadable rows. Nothing is
  written until the maintainer confirms.
- **Re-import is safe (count-based dedup).** `computeExpenseImportPlan` keys on
  `date | merchant | amount | category` and inserts only `max(0, fileCount −
dbCount)` per key, scoping the existing-rows query to the file's date range —
  re-running the same file is a no-op.
- **Architecture mirrors the report** (pure core + imperative shell). Pure:
  `parseExpenseImportCsv` (`src/lib/utils/expenseImportCsv.ts`),
  `computeExpenseImportPlan` + `buildExpenseCategoryLinks`
  (`src/lib/utils/expenseImportPlan.ts`). Shell: `ExpenseImportService`
  (`buildPreview`/`previewFromText` → `commit`). Reuse: the bank-parser CSV
  primitives (tokenizer, date, amount) were **extracted** from `BaseCSVParser`
  into `src/lib/utils/csvPrimitives.ts` (base now delegates; the 7 bank-parser
  suites are the oracle) so the tokenizer isn't duplicated; `ExcelToCSVConverter`
  handles XLS/XLSX.
- **Verification.** 14 tests `expenseImportCsv.spec.ts`, 12
  `expenseImportPlan.spec.ts`, 7 `ExpenseImportService.spec.ts` (a purpose-built
  Supabase fake dispatching by table/op). `check`/eslint/Prettier clean; full
  suite green; the 229 bank-parser tests still pass after the primitive
  extraction. Live end-to-end pass by the maintainer (no auth/seed harness), like
  the earlier slices.

## Deferred (later slices)

- Prior-period overlay line + year-over-year comparison (needs historical data —
  now **unblocked** by the historical upload above).
- ~~Historical-year expense upload~~ — **built ✅** (v0.70), see section above.
- Arbitrary period / quarter selection (beyond a single calendar year).

content.content: 11	- **Spending Report (v1).** New top-level `/spending` tab rolling up Expenses by Importance → Grouping → Category, months across, "Year to Date" total. Adds `importance_areas` + `category_groups` tables (Importance attaches to the Grouping) and `categories.group_id`, seeded from `docs/SampleHierachy.txt`. Client-side pure aggregation (`buildSpendingReport`), view-only, no editing UI. Uncategorized bucket included in Grand Total; refunds (negative amounts) net against spend. **Chart view (v0.60):** `Table | Chart` toggle adds a LayerChart stacked bar (bar per Grouping, stacked by month, sequential ramp; Importance as sub-label; click a bar to drill to Categories, breadcrumb back). Pure `buildSpendingChart`; render-tested. **Table cell drill-down (v0.55) ✅ DONE:** clicking a non-blank table cell opens `/expenses` filtered to exactly what it sums — category×month, category YTD, Grouping/Importance subtotals (expanded to member category ids), Uncategorized (`filter=uncategorized`), and Grand Total (date range only, ties out incl. Uncategorized). Pure `buildSpendingDrilldownParams` (8 tests); report rows/sections now carry ids (`categoryId`/group `id`/importance `id`). **Editable hierarchy — assign & re-parent (v0.65) ✅ DONE:** an **Edit hierarchy** page at `/spending/hierarchy` (button on `/spending`) lets the maintainer assign a Category to a Grouping (or Uncategorized) and move a Grouping to another Importance — closing the "custom/renamed categories stuck in Uncategorized" gap without SQL. Pure `buildHierarchyTree` (8 tests) + presentational `HierarchyEditor.svelte` (5 render tests); `CategoryService.assignCategoryToGroup` / `moveGroupToImportance`. Unassigned bucket surfaced up top. **Assign-on-create (v0.66) ✅ DONE:** the inline "Create new category…" form (expenses page `CategoryDropdown`) offers an optional Group selector so a new category is filed into a Grouping at birth instead of Uncategorized (`createCategory` gained an optional `groupId`; selector hidden when no groups passed, so receipt/reconciliation dropdowns are unchanged). See [Spending Report design](plans/2026-07-09-spending-report-design.md).

Build succeeds (the first failure was just missing PUBLIC env vars — the known 1Password/`.env` behavior). Done.

## Historical-year expense upload — shipped (v0.70)

The keystone slice is built. Users can now import prior years' expenses from a CSV/Excel file with columns `Timestamp, Merchant, Amount, Category` (matching your screenshot), which **unblocks** the year-over-year / prior-period-overlay thread.

**Key decisions that made it clean — no schema change or migration:**
- Imageless receipts already work (`receipt_image_path` nullable, `suspicious_date` forced false), so each row is one `receipts` insert + one `expense_categories` link.
- Your CSV's sign convention (positive = expense, negative = refund) already matches `receipts.total_amount`, so refunds net against spend with **no inversion**.
- Per your three answers: **Tag dropped**, **preview→confirm** step, and new categories land Uncategorized with a **warning + link to the hierarchy editor**.

**What landed:**
| Layer | File | Tests |
|---|---|---|
| Pure parser | `src/lib/utils/expenseImportCsv.ts` | 14 |
| Pure dedup + linking | `src/lib/utils/expenseImportPlan.ts` | 12 |
| Service (shell) | `src/lib/services/ExpenseImportService.ts` | 7 |
| Route + preview UI | `src/routes/expenses/import/+page.svelte` | — |
| Entry points | buttons on `/expenses` and `/spending` | — |

- **DRY refactor:** extracted the CSV tokenizer/date/amount from `BaseCSVParser` into `src/lib/utils/csvPrimitives.ts` (base now delegates) rather than duplicate them — the **229 bank-parser tests are unchanged**, proving behavior-identical.
- **Re-import is safe:** count-based dedup keyed on `date|merchant|amount|category`, scoped to the file's date range.

**Verification:** `npm run check` 0 errors, ESLint + Prettier clean on touched files, full unit suite **1387 passed / 8 skipped** (33 new), production build succeeds. Not exercised: a rendered end-to-end pass — there's no local auth/seed harness, so that's your live-verify step (as with prior slices). Docs (`docs/plans/2026-07-09-spending-report-design.md`, `docs/product-backlog.md`) and `version.ts` updated. Nothing is staged/committed — per your workflow, commits are yours.

**Natural next step:** with historical data now loadable, the **prior-period overlay + year-over-year** slice is unblocked.

One thing to confirm when you try it live: that the `Category` names in your real file resolve against your existing categories as expected — anything unmatched will be auto-created and flagged in the preview, so you'll see it before committing.

Worst case is `PDFExportService.calculateSubtotal` (`src/lib/services/PDFExportService.ts:176`), which *adds* `abs(amount)` — a −$25.50 refund + $100 purchase totals **$125.50** instead of $74.50. The on-screen Spending report is correct (`spendingReport.ts:135` keeps refunds negative) — only the exports diverge. Note: current behaviour is deliberate and locked in by tests (`PDFExportService.spec.ts:199`, `CSVExportService.spec.ts:106`), so a fix must update those too. Low priority.
25	- **Blank transaction date hint.** When the transaction date is blank, show the expected date format for someone who is typing.
26	- **Unknown-sender email is silently dropped.** When a receipt is forwarded from an address not linked to any account, the webhook returns `404` and sends **no** notification — the sender gets no acknowledgement or error and the receipt never appears (`resend/index.ts:378-381`). Resend does not bounce/reply on a webhook error, so any feedback must be an email we send ourselves; deferred because auto-replying to unverified `From:` addresses is a backscatter/spoofing risk (would need SPF/DKIM gating + rate limiting). **End-user docs must flag this:** forward only from a registered email (primary or an additional email in your profile). See [Email notifications — scenario 7](email-notifications.md).

30	- **High vuln: `xlsx` (SheetJS) has no npm fix.** `npm audit` reports 1 high against `xlsx@^0.18.5` — Prototype Pollution ([GHSA-4r6h-8v6p-xvw6](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-4r6h-8v6p-xvw6), CVE-2023-30533, fixed in 0.19.3) and ReDoS ([GHSA-5pgg-2g8v-p4x9](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5pgg-2g8v-p4x9), CVE-2024-22363, fixed in 0.20.2). Both fixes exist but **only on the SheetJS CDN (`cdn.sheetjs.com`), not npm** — the npm package is unmaintained, so `npm audit` will never clear and there's no fix version to bump to. Used only by the Excel importer, fully contained in `src/lib/services/ExcelToCSVConverter.ts` (`convertExcelToCSV`/`isExcelFile`, ~4 API calls) behind a stable interface; the app supports **both** legacy `.xls` (BIFF8) and `.xlsx` (tests build both, `ExcelToCSVConverter.test.ts`). Options: (a) pin the CDN tarball (`xlsx@https://cdn.sheetjs.com/xlsx-0.20.3/...` via `overrides`) — clears the CVEs, keeps `.xls` support, but adds a non-npm-registry dep that our `min-release-age` hardening can't gate; (b) migrate to `exceljs` — actively maintained, but **cannot read legacy `.xls`** (xlsx/csv only), so it would drop `.xls` support unless paired with a dedicated BIFF parser (`js-xls`). Decision needed on whether legacy `.xls` is still required. Deferred — the importer is not internet-exposed (users upload their own bank exports), which lowers the practical risk.

content.text: Both issues are on the Spending page's state/loading. Let me read the full page to see how `year` drives loading and whether it's persisted.

Both symptoms share one root cause: **`year` is component-local `$state`, never persisted.** On any remount — SPA navigation back to the tab *or* a full browser refresh — it resets to the current year (2026). Since your imported data is 2025, a refresh/return drops you on empty 2026 ("table doesn't get rebuilt") and loses the selected year.

The fix is to persist `year` in the URL, matching the codebase's "filters preserved in URL" pattern. Let me see how the expenses page updates URL params to stay consistent:

content.text:
Fixed. Both symptoms had one root cause and one fix.

## What was wrong

`year` was component-local `$state(new Date().getFullYear())`, persisted nowhere. Any remount reset it to the current year (2026):
- **"Lost the year on return"** — SPA-navigating back to `/spending` remounts the component → year snaps to 2026.
- **"Table doesn't rebuild after a refresh"** — a full reload also remounts → 2026, which has no data (your imported expenses are 2025), so the grid comes up empty.

## The fix — year encoded in the URL

- On mount, the year is read from `/spending?year=2025` via a pure `parseYearParam(searchParams, fallbackYear)` (falls back to the current year for a missing/garbage/out-of-range value).
- `changeYear` writes it back with `replaceState` (no navigation, no remount), matching the expenses page's URL-persistence pattern.

Now a refresh, a Back from a drill-down, or a tab round-trip all restore the selected year and rebuild the grid for it.

**Files:** `src/lib/utils/spendingYear.ts` (+ 6 tests), `src/routes/spending/+page.svelte`, `version.ts` → `0.71`, design doc.
**Verification:** `npm run check` 0/0, ESLint + Prettier clean, new unit tests pass, production build succeeds. As before, there's no auth/seed harness for a rendered end-to-end pass — worth a quick live check: set a past year, refresh, and confirm the grid comes back on that year.

One related thing I *didn't* change: the `Table | Chart` view toggle is also component-local and resets to Table on remount. Not reported, so I left it — say the word if you'd like it persisted the same way.
URL Says 2025 - Table displayed is 2026:

The URL has `year=2025` but the grid shows 2026 — so my read-once-in-`onMount` approach isn't reliably reflecting the URL. The robust fix (and the pattern this codebase already uses — the expenses page derives its date filter from `$page.url.searchParams`) is to make `year` **derived from the URL** and reload via an effect, so the URL is the single source of truth. Let me read the current page and refactor.

Found it. `onMount` is `async` and only sets `year` *after* two `await`s — but more fundamentally, reading the URL once is fragile. The proven pattern here (expenses page, line 89) is to **derive** state from `$page.url.searchParams` so it always tracks the URL, and reload via an `$effect`. Let me refactor to that:

content.text:
Build succeeds. Here's what changed and why it's now correct.

## Why the URL said 2025 but the grid showed 2026

My first fix read the URL **once**, late inside an `async onMount` — only *after* awaiting `getSession()` and `getDefaultFamilyId()`. That both raced the initial render and left `year` as ordinary `$state`, so nothing kept it tied to the address bar. The result: `year` could stay at its 2026 initializer while the URL said 2025.

## The real fix — URL is the single source of truth

`year` is now **derived** from the URL, exactly like the expenses page derives its date filter:

```ts
let year = $derived(parseYearParam($page.url.searchParams, currentYear));
```

- A reload `$effect` fires whenever the derived `year` **or** the resolved `familyId` changes → rebuilds the report for that year.
- `changeYear` just writes `?year=` to the URL (`replaceState`); the derived `year` and the effect follow. No manual reload, no state that can drift from the URL.

So now the header year, the loaded data, and the address bar are always the same value — on refresh, on Back from a drill-down, and on returning to the tab.

**Files:** `src/routes/spending/+page.svelte`, `version.ts` → `0.72`, design doc. The pure `parseYearParam` + its 6 tests from before still apply.
**Verified:** `check` 0/0, ESLint + Prettier clean, production build succeeds.

Please reload `localhost:5173/spending?year=2025` (a full refresh, to clear any HMR-preserved state from the earlier version) — the header and grid should both show 2025 now, and clicking the arrows should keep the URL and display in sync.
Only increment the version if the app has been committed and pushed to live.

name: feedback_version_bump_only_on_commit
description: Only bump src/lib/version.ts when the change is actually committed & pushed live
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

Do **not** increment `APP_VERSION` in `src/lib/version.ts` for uncommitted work.
Only bump the version when the app has been committed and pushed to live. While
building/iterating (which may span several turns before a commit), leave the
version at its current committed value.

**Why:** the LLM never commits (see [[feedback_no_git_commit]]); the human commits
and pushes. Bumping the version on every uncommitted edit desyncs the displayed
version from what's actually live and burns version numbers on work that may still
change.

**How to apply:** when finishing a feature/fix, leave `version.ts` alone. In docs
(design docs, product-backlog) don't assert a specific version tag (e.g. "v0.70")
for unreleased work — write "(pending release)" / "version assigned on commit"
instead. The human assigns and bumps the version at commit time.

1	- [No git commits by LLM](feedback_no_git_commit.md) — Only the human creates git commits, never the LLM
2	- [No browser console reliance](feedback_no_console_reliance.md) — Console output is for debugging only; user-facing info must appear in the UI
3	- [No confirm() for reversible actions](feedback_no_confirm_for_reversible.md) — Skip confirm prompts on reversible toggles (exclude/include, match/unmatch); keep them for deletes
4	- [No Mistral in unit tests](feedback_no_mistral_in_tests.md) — Tests must never call the OCR API; assert prompt constants, keep logic pure, mock fetch
5	- [OCR & upload resilience](feedback_ocr_resilience.md) — Upload pipeline must survive Mistral outages; no orphan storage files; render-time formatters must fail soft
6	- [No `any` even in tests](feedback_no_any_in_tests.md) — Prefer typed mocks/Partial/MockedFunction; `as any` is last-resort with a reason, not the default
7	- [Code style: returns](feedback_code_style_returns.md) — Guard clauses good; heterogeneous union return types bad (high pri); forced `T|null` tolerated (low pri)
8	- [a11y labels & Prettier shorthand](project_a11y_label_and_prettier_shorthand.md) — for/id vs wrap-component vs span for labels; flowbite Datepicker doesn't forward id; Prettier shorthand can break source-regex tests
9	- [Fix warnings in touched files](feedback_fix_warnings_in_touched_files.md) — When editing a file, clear its pre-existing lint/type warnings too, not just note them
10	- [Validate characterization tests with an oracle](feedback_validate_characterization_tests_with_oracle.md) — For extract-refactors, run the original code verbatim as an oracle to prove hand-authored test expectations are correct
11	- [Playwright is seam-only](feedback_testing_pyramid_playwright_seam_only.md) — Unit tests own correctness; Playwright only proves the UI is wired to the tested logic (one thin flow, no boundary matrices). No auth/seed harness exists yet.
12	- [No repo-wide format](feedback_no_repo_wide_format.md) — Never run `npm run format` (prettier --write .); format only touched files with `npx prettier --write <files>`

14	- [Spec system is dead](project_spec_system_dead.md) — specs/specifications, `#{#id}` tags, and spec:validate are abandoned leftovers despite CLAUDE.md; write plain PRDs, no new tags

## Gotchas

- Dual test environments: browser tests use Playwright provider, server tests use Node.js — configured in `vite.config.ts` under `test.projects`
- PDFs go directly to Mistral Vision API (pixtral-12b) — no conversion needed
- Suspicious date flag triggers for receipts >42 days old or future-dated
- Multi-email support: primary email in `auth.users`, up to 5 additional in `profiles` table. Email receipt ingestion checks both.
- File uploads: JPEG/PNG/HEIC up to 5MB, PDF up to 10MB. Validated client-side and server-side (`src/lib/server/fileValidation.ts`)
- Recent migrations (Jan–Feb 2026) refactored family-scoping, fixed RLS recursion issues, and secured storage — be careful modifying RLS policies
- Receipt image URLs are async (signed URLs). Components use `$effect` + `Promise.then()` to load them, not synchronous calls. Never use `getPublicUrl()`.

When a page's reactive state is **derived from the URL** (query params), derive it
off the **`$app/state`** reactive `page` object, not the legacy `$app/stores`
`$page` store:

```ts
import { page } from '$app/state';
let year = $derived(parseYearParam(page.url.searchParams, currentYear));
```

remount — e.g. navigate `/spending?year=2025` → drill into an expense → browser
Back → URL says 2025 but the grid renders the current year. The `$page` store
doesn't reliably re-track inside `$derived` across a remount in Svelte 5 runes.
`$app/state`'s `page` is a `$state`-backed reactive object built for runes and
updates on every navigation (incl. back/forward), so it fixes both the remount
and component-reuse cases. kit ≥ 2.12 (repo is on 2.63).

Pattern in `/spending`: URL is the single source of truth — `year` derived from
`page.url`, a reload `$effect` fires on `year`/`familyId` change, and the year
buttons just `replaceState('/spending?year=…')`. See
docs/plans/2026-07-09-spending-report-design.md.

`$derived(readDateFilter($page.url.searchParams))` with the `$app/stores` store —
same shape, so it may have the same Back-navigation staleness. Not yet reported;
worth converting if it surfaces.

content.text:
Fixed the actual root cause this time.

## What was really wrong

The header binds `{year}`, and it showed 2026 — so the **derived `year` itself** was computing the current year, meaning `$page.url.searchParams` didn't reflect `?year=2025` after Back. The culprit is a Svelte 5 reactivity gotcha: the **legacy `$app/stores` `$page` store doesn't reliably re-track inside `$derived` across a remount** (which is exactly what Back-from-a-drill-down causes). My previous derived fix was right in shape but built on the wrong `page` source.

## The fix

Switched the source to the **Svelte 5 reactive `page` from `$app/state`**:

```ts
import { page } from '$app/state';
let year = $derived(parseYearParam(page.url.searchParams, currentYear));
```

`$app/state`'s `page` is a `$state`-backed reactive object designed for runes; it updates on every navigation including back/forward, so the derived `year` now tracks the URL through remounts. The reload `$effect` and the `replaceState`-only year buttons are unchanged. Available in kit 2.12+ (you're on 2.63).

**Verified:** `check` 0/0, ESLint + Prettier clean, production build succeeds. `version.ts` stays at the committed `0.68` per your rule.

Please give it a full reload and re-run your exact repro: `…/spending?year=2025` → click an uncategorized expense → Back. The grid should now come back on 2025.

**One thing to flag:** `src/routes/expenses/+page.svelte` uses the *same* pattern — `$derived(readDateFilter($page.url.searchParams))` off the legacy `$app/stores` store — so it likely has the same latent Back-navigation staleness on its date filters. It's not something you reported, so I didn't touch it, but I recorded it (and this whole gotcha) in memory. Want me to convert the expenses page to `$app/state` too?
