28	## Engineering
29	
30	- **High vuln: `xlsx` (SheetJS) has no npm fix.** `npm audit` reports 1 high against `xlsx@^0.18.5` — Prototype Pollution ([GHSA-4r6h-8v6p-xvw6](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-4r6h-8v6p-xvw6), CVE-2023-30533, fixed in 0.19.3) and ReDoS ([GHSA-5pgg-2g8v-p4x9](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5pgg-2g8v-p4x9), CVE-2024-22363, fixed in 0.20.2). Both fixes exist but **only on the SheetJS CDN (`cdn.sheetjs.com`), not npm** — the npm package is unmaintained, so `npm audit` will never clear and there's no fix version to bump to. Used only by the Excel importer, fully contained in `src/lib/services/ExcelToCSVConverter.ts` (`convertExcelToCSV`/`isExcelFile`, ~4 API calls) behind a stable interface; the app supports **both** legacy `.xls` (BIFF8) and `.xlsx` (tests build both, `ExcelToCSVConverter.test.ts`). Options: (a) pin the CDN tarball (`xlsx@https://cdn.sheetjs.com/xlsx-0.20.3/...` via `overrides`) — clears the CVEs, keeps `.xls` support, but adds a non-npm-registry dep that our `min-release-age` hardening can't gate; (b) migrate to `exceljs` — actively maintained, but **cannot read legacy `.xls`** (xlsx/csv only), so it would drop `.xls` support unless paired with a dedicated BIFF parser (`js-xls`). Decision needed on whether legacy `.xls` is still required. Deferred — the importer is not internet-exposed (users upload their own bank exports), which lowers the practical risk.
31	- **Low vulns: `cookie` (via `@sveltejs/kit`) and `esbuild` dev server.** `npm audit` reports 6 low-severity issues. (1) `cookie <0.7.0` accepts out-of-bounds characters in name/path/domain ([GHSA-pxg6-pf52-xh8x](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-pxg6-pf52-xh8x)), pulled in transitively through `@sveltejs/kit` → `@sveltejs/adapter-auto` / `runed` / `layerchart`; `npm audit fix --force` would downgrade `@sveltejs/kit` to `1.0.0-next.0` (breaking), so wait for the framework chain to bump `cookie` rather than force it. (2) `esbuild 0.27.3–0.28.0` allows arbitrary file read when the dev server runs on Windows ([GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr)) — dev-only, non-Windows here; clearable with a plain `npm audit fix` (non-breaking). Low priority; both are dev/transitive, not shipped to users.
32	- **`insert_receipt_with_context` RPC drops columns.** The RPC inserts only 9 columns and silently omits `suspicious_date` and `exchange_rate_to_cad` (`supabase/migrations/003_insert_receipt_rpc.sql`, and again in `20251010000319_remote_schema.sql`). The Resend email path passes both, so emailed receipts lose their suspicious-date flag and FX rate on the primary path (they only survive if the RPC errors into the direct-insert fallback). Fix: add both columns to the RPC insert (new migration) and confirm the remote function matches. Found while fixing the email-receipt null-date bug.
33	- **Test the Resend webhook handler. ✅ DONE.** `handleResendWebhook(req, deps)` extracted from `Deno.serve` into `supabase/functions/resend/handler.ts` (functional core) with `index.ts` reduced to the dep-wiring shell; `notify.ts` / `mistral.ts` / `exchangeRate.ts` gained optional `fetchFn`/`env` seams. The full branch matrix (rows 1–20: auth gates, body/attachment/fallback flow, notify-on-failure, foreign-currency) is covered in `handler.test.ts` (20 vitest cases, no network/Supabase/Deno). `deno check` clean on all production files. See [PRD — Make the Resend webhook handler testable](prd-resend-handler-testability.md).

Used only by the Excel importer, fully contained in `src/lib/services/ExcelToCSVConverter.ts` (`convertExcelToCSV`/`isExcelFile`, ~4 API calls) behind a stable interface; the app supports **both** legacy `.xls` (BIFF8) and `.xlsx` (tests build both, `ExcelToCSVConverter.test.ts`). Options: (a) pin the CDN tarball (`xlsx@https://cdn.sheetjs.com/xlsx-0.20.3/...` via `overrides`) — clears the CVEs, keeps `.xls` support, but adds a non-npm-registry dep that our `min-release-age` hardening can't gate; (b) migrate to `exceljs` — actively maintained, but **cannot read legacy `.xls`** (xlsx/csv only), so it would drop `.xls` support unless paired with a dedicated BIFF parser (`js-xls`). Decision needed on whether legacy `.xls` is still required. Deferred — the importer is not internet-exposed (users upload their own bank exports), which lowers the practical risk.

- **Low vulns: `cookie` (via `@sveltejs/kit`) and `esbuild` dev server.** `npm audit` reports 6 low-severity issues. (1) `cookie <0.7.0` accepts out-of-bounds characters in name/path/domain ([GHSA-pxg6-pf52-xh8x](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-pxg6-pf52-xh8x)), pulled in transitively through `@sveltejs/kit` → `@sveltejs/adapter-auto` / `runed` / `layerchart`; `npm audit fix --force` would downgrade `@sveltejs/kit` to `1.0.0-next.0` (breaking), so wait for the framework chain to bump `cookie` rather than force it. (2) `esbuild 0.27.3–0.28.0` allows arbitrary file read when the dev server runs on Windows ([GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr)) — dev-only, non-Windows here; clearable with a plain `npm audit fix` (non-breaking). Low priority; both are dev/transitive, not shipped to users.

+- **Expenses page: date filter may go stale on Back nav (legacy `$page` store).** `src/routes/expenses/+page.svelte` derives its date filter from the URL via `$derived(readDateFilter($page.url.searchParams))` using the **legacy `$app/stores` `$page` store**. That's the same pattern that broke the Spending year selector: the `$page` store doesn't reliably re-track inside `$derived` across a remount, so after navigating away and pressing **Back** the URL can say one date range while the page renders another. Spending was fixed by deriving off the **`$app/state` reactive `page`** object (`import { page } from '$app/state'`; drop the `$`). Apply the same one-line-ish swap to the expenses page (and audit any other `$derived(... $page.url ...)` sites). Not yet reproduced/reported for expenses — latent. See the Spending report design doc and the `$app/state`-in-`$derived` note.

- **`insert_receipt_with_context` RPC drops columns.** The RPC inserts only 9 columns and silently omits `suspicious_date` and `exchange_rate_to_cad` (`supabase/migrations/003_insert_receipt_rpc.sql`, and again in `20251010000319_remote_schema.sql`). The Resend email path passes both, so emailed receipts lose their suspicious-date flag and FX rate on the primary path (they only survive if the RPC errors into the direct-insert fallback). Fix: add both columns to the RPC insert (new migration) and confirm the remote function matches. Found while fixing the email-receipt null-date bug.

- **Test the Resend webhook handler. ✅ DONE.** `handleResendWebhook(req, deps)` extracted from `Deno.serve` into `supabase/functions/resend/handler.ts` (functional core) with `index.ts` reduced to the dep-wiring shell; `notify.ts` / `mistral.ts` / `exchangeRate.ts` gained optional `fetchFn`/`env` seams. The full branch matrix (rows 1–20: auth gates, body/attachment/fallback flow, notify-on-failure, foreign-currency) is covered in `handler.test.ts` (20 vitest cases, no network/Supabase/Deno). `deno check` clean on all production files. See [PRD — Make the Resend webhook handler testable](prd-resend-handler-testability.md).

- **PRD correction: Resend "no receipt" status is 422, not 404.** The testability PRD's §5 test plan lists `404` for row 18 (nothing found anywhere), but the deployed handler returns `422` — `404` is reserved for the unknown-sender case (row 10). The tests assert the real `422` (zero-behaviour-change goal); the PRD table row is the doc that's wrong. Low priority: fix the PRD table or leave the note.

content.text:
Root cause confirmed: `buildExpenseQuery` has no `.range()`/pagination, so Supabase caps at 1000 rows. `getExpenses(userId)` (no filters) loads only the newest 1000 receipts; after a large import, the drilled 2025 rows aren't among them — and the **Spending report undercounts** any year over 1000 rows too. Fix: paginate `getExpenses` to fetch all matching rows.

lines: - **High vuln: `xlsx` (SheetJS) has no npm fix.** `npm audit` reports 1 high against `xlsx@^0.18.5` — Prototype Pollution ([GHSA-4r6h-8v6p-xvw6](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-4r6h-8v6p-xvw6), CVE-2023-30533, fixed in 0.19.3) and ReDoS ([GHSA-5pgg-2g8v-p4x9](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5pgg-2g8v-p4x9), CVE-2024-22363, fixed in 0.20.2). Both fixes exist but **only on the SheetJS CDN (`cdn.sheetjs.com`), not npm** — the npm package is unmaintained, so `npm audit` will never clear and there's no fix version to bump to. Used only by the Excel importer, fully contained in `src/lib/services/ExcelToCSVConverter.ts` (`convertExcelToCSV`/`isExcelFile`, ~4 API calls) behind a stable interface; the app supports **both** legacy `.xls` (BIFF8) and `.xlsx` (tests build both, `ExcelToCSVConverter.test.ts`). Options: (a) pin the CDN tarball (`xlsx@https://cdn.sheetjs.com/xlsx-0.20.3/...` via `overrides`) — clears the CVEs, keeps `.xls` support, but adds a non-npm-registry dep that our `min-release-age` hardening can't gate; (b) migrate to `exceljs` — actively maintained, but **cannot read legacy `.xls`** (xlsx/csv only), so it would drop `.xls` support unless paired with a dedicated BIFF parser (`js-xls`). Decision needed on whether legacy `.xls` is still required. Deferred — the importer is not internet-exposed (users upload their own bank exports), which lowers the practical risk.

- **Low vulns: `cookie` (via `@sveltejs/kit`) and `esbuild` dev server.** `npm audit` reports 6 low-severity issues. (1) `cookie <0.7.0` accepts out-of-bounds characters in name/path/domain ([GHSA-pxg6-pf52-xh8x](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-pxg6-pf52-xh8x)), pulled in transitively through `@sveltejs/kit` → `@sveltejs/adapter-auto` / `runed` / `layerchart`; `npm audit fix --force` would downgrade `@sveltejs/kit` to `1.0.0-next.0` (breaking), so wait for the framework chain to bump `cookie` rather than force it. (2) `esbuild 0.27.3–0.28.0` allows arbitrary file read when the dev server runs on Windows ([GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr)) — dev-only, non-Windows here; clearable with a plain `npm audit fix` (non-breaking). Low priority; both are dev/transitive, not shipped to users.

+- **Expenses list capped at 1000 rows (large imports). ✅ DONE.** `ExpenseService.getExpenses` issued a single PostgREST query with no paging, so Supabase's default 1000-row cap silently truncated the result. After the historical importer added thousands of receipts, the expenses page (which loads all expenses then filters client-side) only held the newest 1000 — a Spending-report drill-down into an older year landed on "No results found — hiding all 1000 expenses", and the Spending report itself undercounted any year over 1000 rows. Fixed by paging `getExpenses` in 1000-row `.range()` batches until a short page (`fetchAllReceiptRows`); the shared Supabase mock gained `range`; 2 new pagination tests in `ExpenseService.getExpenses.spec.ts`. Reported via a `/spending` uncategorized drill-down.

- **Expenses page: date filter may go stale on Back nav (legacy `$page` store).** `src/routes/expenses/+page.svelte` derives its date filter from the URL via `$derived(readDateFilter($page.url.searchParams))` using the **legacy `$app/stores` `$page` store**. See the Spending report design doc and the `$app/state`-in-`$derived` note.

The Resend email path passes both, so emailed receipts lose their suspicious-date flag and FX rate on the primary path (they only survive if the RPC errors into the direct-insert fallback). content.text:
Fixed — this was a genuine data-truncation bug, not the year issue.

## Root cause

`ExpenseService.getExpenses` ran a single query with **no pagination**, so Supabase's default **1000-row cap** silently truncated the result. The expenses page loads *all* expenses (`getExpenses(userId)`, no filters) and filters client-side — so after your large import it only ever held the newest 1000 receipts. Your 2025 uncategorized rows (Dental and Vision, Car insurance, Gas, …) weren't among that 1000, so the drill-down landed on "**hiding all 1000 expenses**". Same cap meant the **Spending report was undercounting** any year with over 1000 rows.

## The fix

`getExpenses` now pages through the full result set in 1000-row `.range()` batches until a short page (`fetchAllReceiptRows`), returning every matching row:

```ts
for (let from = 0; ; from += PAGE_SIZE) {
  const { data, error } = await this.buildExpenseQuery(filters).range(from, from + PAGE_SIZE - 1);
  ...
  if (batch.length < PAGE_SIZE) break;
}
```

This fixes both symptoms at the source — the drill-down now finds the rows, **and** the Spending report totals are complete for years over 1000 rows.

**Files:** `ExpenseService.ts` (paginate), `supabaseMock.ts` (added `range` — additive, no existing suite broke), `ExpenseService.getExpenses.spec.ts` (2 pagination tests), backlog note.
**Verified:** `check` 0/0, ESLint + Prettier clean, full suite **1395 passed / 8 skipped**, production build succeeds. `version.ts` untouched at `0.68` per your rule.

Please reload and retry the drill-through on those uncategorized rows — they should now show their receipts. As a knock-on, your Spending grand total may tick **up** slightly if any 2025 month was previously truncated at the cap.

Two related notes worth your awareness (not changed):
- The expenses page still fetches the entire set and filters in the browser. Pagination makes it *correct*, but a few thousand rows is now the client's working set; if it ever gets sluggish, the real remedy is pushing the date/category filters server-side. I can log that as a perf follow-up if you'd like.
- The `matchStatus`/reconciliation and other `getExpenses` callers benefit from the same fix automatically.

9	## Features
10	
11	- **Spending Report (v1).** New top-level `/spending` tab rolling up Expenses by Importance → Grouping → Category, months across, "Year to Date" total. Adds `importance_areas` + `category_groups` tables (Importance attaches to the Grouping) and `categories.group_id`, seeded from `docs/SampleHierachy.txt`. Client-side pure aggregation (`buildSpendingReport`), view-only, no editing UI. Uncategorized bucket included in Grand Total; refunds (negative amounts) net against spend. **Chart view (v0.60):** `Table | Chart` toggle adds a LayerChart stacked bar (bar per Grouping, stacked by month, sequential ramp; Importance as sub-label; click a bar to drill to Categories, breadcrumb back). Pure `buildSpendingChart`; render-tested. **Table cell drill-down (v0.55) ✅ DONE:** clicking a non-blank table cell opens `/expenses` filtered to exactly what it sums — category×month, category YTD, Grouping/Importance subtotals (expanded to member category ids), Uncategorized (`filter=uncategorized`), and Grand Total (date range only, ties out incl. Uncategorized). Pure `buildSpendingDrilldownParams` (8 tests); report rows/sections now carry ids (`categoryId`/group `id`/importance `id`). **Editable hierarchy — assign & re-parent (v0.65) ✅ DONE:** an **Edit hierarchy** page at `/spending/hierarchy` (button on `/spending`) lets the maintainer assign a Category to a Grouping (or Uncategorized) and move a Grouping to another Importance — closing the "custom/renamed categories stuck in Uncategorized" gap without SQL. Pure `buildHierarchyTree` (8 tests) + presentational `HierarchyEditor.svelte` (5 render tests); `CategoryService.assignCategoryToGroup` / `moveGroupToImportance`. Unassigned bucket surfaced up top. **Assign-on-create (v0.66) ✅ DONE:** the inline "Create new category…" form (expenses page `CategoryDropdown`) offers an optional Group selector so a new category is filed into a Grouping at birth instead of Uncategorized (`createCategory` gained an optional `groupId`; selector hidden when no groups passed, so receipt/reconciliation dropdowns are unchanged). **Historical-year expense upload (built, pending release) ✅ DONE:** an **Import Expenses** page at `/expenses/import` (buttons on `/expenses` and `/spending`) imports historical Expenses from CSV/XLS/XLSX (columns `Timestamp, Merchant, Amount, Category`; `Tag` ignored; Amount keeps its sign so refunds net). Each row → an imageless `receipts` row (no schema change — `receipt_image_path` nullable, `suspicious_date` false) + an `expense_categories` link; new category names are auto-created (land Uncategorized, warned in the preview). Two-step **preview → confirm** with count-based dedup (`date|merchant|amount|category`) so re-import is a no-op. Pure `parseExpenseImportCsv` (14) + `computeExpenseImportPlan`/`buildExpenseCategoryLinks` (12) + `ExpenseImportService` (7); the bank-parser CSV primitives were extracted to `csvPrimitives.ts` (base delegates; 229 parser tests unchanged). This **unblocks** prior-period overlay + year-over-year. Deferred: **chart-bar drill-down** (same affordance on the chart bars — carry the cell-link into `/expenses` from a bar/bracket click); **hierarchy tier CRUD** (create/rename/delete/reorder Groupings + Importance areas, with cascade-delete confirmations); prior-period overlay + year-over-year (now unblocked), quarter/period selection, multi-chart menu, export. See [Spending Report design](plans/2026-07-09-spending-report-design.md).
12	- **Delete a category.** Let the maintainer delete a category, likely from the hierarchy editor (`/spending/hierarchy`). Needs a decision on what happens to expenses still linked to it (block delete while in use, or reassign to Uncategorized) and cascade handling of vendor rules / `expense_categories` links; a confirm is warranted since delete is destructive.
13	- **Mass-change categories on the expenses page.** Select multiple expenses on `/expenses` and re-categorize them in one action (bulk assign). Needs row selection (checkboxes + select-all), a bulk "Set category…" control, and a single batched update across the selected `expense_categories` links.
14	- **Receipt image — rotate.** Rotate left and right anywhere a receipt is viewed.
15	- **Profile — manage emails.** Let users add/edit the email addresses associated with their account.
16	- **Family editor.** Let a user create a family and then invite other users to join it.
17	- **iPhone camera.** Use the Camera app on iPhone to take photos of receipts.
18	- **Recent-categories dropdown & a11y _(optional UX, low priority)_.** Recent-categories dropdown section (exp2b), mobile-responsive category dropdown (exp8a), and category-dropdown ARIA/screen-reader support (exp8b) were specced but never built.
19	- **Specced-but-unbuilt UX bits _(optional, low priority)_.** Email-flow vendor auto-assignment (vca2a email path) and the read-only "Rate: 1 EUR = …" text in the receipt edit modal (fcr2b) were specced but not implemented.

21	## Bugs / UX issues
22	
23	- **Receipt with No Date** - if a receipt has no date it is hard to find in the receipts view.
24	- **Category edit scrolls to top.** When a category is edited we always scroll back up to the top of the window.
25	- **Category dropdown clipped.** The category dropdown in the editor window is out of view when clicked.
26	- **Refunds counted as spending in PDF/CSV exports.** The PDF and CSV exporters `Math.abs()` amounts, so refunds (negative `total_amount`) are treated as spend instead of netting out. Worst case is `PDFExportService.calculateSubtotal` (`src/lib/services/PDFExportService.ts:176`), which *adds* `abs(amount)` — a −$25.50 refund + $100 purchase totals **$125.50** instead of $74.50. The display formatters also strip the sign (`PDFExportService.ts:126`, `CSVExportService.ts:134`), so an exported refund prints as a positive purchase. The on-screen Spending report is correct (`spendingReport.ts:135` keeps refunds negative) — only the exports diverge. Note: current behaviour is deliberate and locked in by tests (`PDFExportService.spec.ts:199`, `CSVExportService.spec.ts:106`), so a fix must update those too. Low priority.
27	- **Blank transaction date hint.** When the transaction date is blank, show the expected date format for someone who is typing.
28	- **Unknown-sender email is silently dropped.** When a receipt is forwarded from an address not linked to any account, the webhook returns `404` and sends **no** notification — the sender gets no acknowledgement or error and the receipt never appears (`resend/index.ts:378-381`). Resend does not bounce/reply on a webhook error, so any feedback must be an email we send ourselves; deferred because auto-replying to unverified `From:` addresses is a backscatter/spoofing risk (would need SPF/DKIM gating + rate limiting). **End-user docs must flag this:** forward only from a registered email (primary or an additional email in your profile). See [Email notifications — scenario 7](email-notifications.md).

---
name: reference_app_state_page_in_derived
description: For URL-backed page state that must survive Back/refresh, read it in a +page.ts load, not a client-side $derived off the page store
metadata:
  type: reference
---

For page state that is **backed by the URL** (query params) and must survive a
browser **Back**, a refresh, and same-route navigation, read it in a **`+page.ts`
`load`** and consume `data.x` — do NOT derive it client-side from the page store.

```ts
// +page.ts
export const load: PageLoad = ({ url }) => ({ year: parseYearParam(url.searchParams, new Date().getFullYear()) });
```
```svelte
let { data }: { data: PageData } = $props();
let year = $derived(data.year);
function changeYear(d) { goto(resolve(`/spending?year=${year + d}`), { replaceState: true, keepFocus: true, noScroll: true }); }
```

**Why:** `load` re-runs with the correct `url` on every navigation (arrows via
`goto`, Back, refresh), so `data.year` is always in lock-step with `?year=`.
Changing the URL for the arrows must use **`goto`** (re-runs `load`), NOT
`replaceState` (shallow routing — doesn't re-run `load`, so the arrows looked
inert).

**What failed in `/spending` (don't retry these):**
1. Read the URL once in `onMount` → raced the initial render.
2. `$derived(readDateFilter($page.url.searchParams))` off the **`$app/stores`
   `$page` store** → stale year after Back.
3. `$derived(... page.url ...)` off the **`$app/state` reactive `page`** PLUS
   `replaceState`-driven arrows → STILL stale on Back, and the arrows didn't
   navigate. So `$app/state` alone is not a reliable fix for the Back case here.

Only the `load` approach held up. See docs/plans/2026-07-09-spending-report-design.md.

**Latent risk:** `src/routes/expenses/+page.svelte` still derives its date filter
from `$app/stores` `$page` in `$derived` — same class of bug, may go stale on
Back. Logged in the product backlog; convert to a `load` if it surfaces.

---
name: reference_app_state_page_in_derived
description: "Derive URL-backed state from $app/state page, not the legacy $app/stores $page store"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: c5bbfa7b-b74f-412a-8f4c-ac216182af79
---

When a page's reactive state is **derived from the URL** (query params), derive it
off the **`$app/state`** reactive `page` object, not the legacy `$app/stores`
`$page` store:

```ts
import { page } from '$app/state';
let year = $derived(parseYearParam(page.url.searchParams, currentYear));
```

**Symptom of getting it wrong:** with `import { page } from '$app/stores'` and
`$derived(... $page.url ...)`, the derived value shows a **stale** URL after a
remount — e.g. navigate `/spending?year=2025` → drill into an expense → browser
Back → URL says 2025 but the grid renders the current year. The `$page` store
doesn't reliably re-track inside `$derived` across a remount in Svelte 5 runes.
`$app/state`'s `page` is a `$state`-backed reactive object built for runes and
updates on every navigation (incl. back/forward), so it fixes both the remount
and component-reuse cases. kit ≥ 2.12 (repo is on 2.63).

Pattern in `/spending`: URL is the single source of truth — `year` derived from
`page.url`, a reload `$effect` fires on `year`/`familyId` change, and the year
buttons just `replaceState('/spending?year=…')`. See
docs/plans/2026-07-09-spending-report-design.md.

**Latent risk:** `src/routes/expenses/+page.svelte` still does
`$derived(readDateFilter($page.url.searchParams))` with the `$app/stores` store —
same shape, so it may have the same Back-navigation staleness. Not yet reported;
worth converting if it surfaces.

content.text:
Both problems fixed, and this time the fix is structurally different — it doesn't rely on client-side reactivity that can go stale.

## Why the last two attempts failed

Both symptoms traced to reading the year from client-side page reactivity:
- **Arrows dead:** `changeYear` used `replaceState` (shallow routing), which doesn't re-run anything — so nothing recomputed the year.
- **Back showed 2026:** deriving `year` from the page store — first `$app/stores` `$page`, then even `$app/state` `page` — went stale when the component remounted on Back.

## The fix: read the year in a `+page.ts` `load`

`load` is the one thing SvelteKit **guarantees to re-run with the correct URL on every navigation** — arrows, Back, and refresh alike. So the year can't drift from the URL.

- **`src/routes/spending/+page.ts`** (new): `load({ url }) → { year: parseYearParam(url.searchParams, currentYear) }`.
- **`+page.svelte`**: `let { data } = $props()`, `year = $derived(data.year)`; the reload `$effect` fires when `data.year` changes.
- **Arrows** now use `goto('?year=…', { replaceState: true, keepFocus: true, noScroll: true })` — `goto` re-runs `load`, so `data.year` updates and the report reloads. `replaceState: true` keeps the back-stack clean (Back returns to where you came from, not through each year you clicked).

Net: URL → `load` → `data.year` → report, on every navigation. Back from a drill-down re-runs `load` with `?year=2025` and lands on 2025; the arrows navigate and reload.

**Files:** `+page.ts` (new), `+page.svelte`, design doc, backlog, memory. The pure `parseYearParam` + its 6 tests still back it (now consumed by `load`).
**Verified:** `check` 0/0, ESLint + Prettier clean, production build succeeds. `version.ts` stays at committed `0.68`.

I've been wrong twice here, so please re-run your exact repro to confirm: load `…/spending?year=2025` → click an uncategorized expense → Back (should show 2025), and click the ← / → arrows (should change the year and reload). If anything's still off, tell me and I'll dig in further rather than guess.
How much complexity have we added?
Fair question — let me measure it rather than guess.

content.text:
Here's an honest accounting.

## Raw numbers
- **New production code:** ~1,000 lines across 7 files
- **New tests:** ~535 lines (33 tests)
- **Changed existing files:** net **−59 lines** (the CSV-primitives extraction deleted more than it added)

## Where the complexity actually went

**Essential — the historical importer (~800 prod + ~500 test).** This is genuinely new capability: parse → dedup → create receipts + categories + links → preview UI. It follows the codebase's existing pure-core/imperative-shell shape, so it adds *volume* but not *novelty*. Hard to do meaningfully cheaper.

**Roughly neutral — CSV primitives extraction.** `BaseCSVParser` shrank ~170 lines; `csvPrimitives.ts` added ~190. It removed duplication (the tokenizer isn't copy-pasted) at the cost of one layer of indirection (base now delegates). Net wash, arguably a small win.

**Small but real — the year-in-URL + pagination fixes.** The final Spending fix is tiny (a 16-line `load` + `goto`). But two things there increased moving parts:

1. **The Spending page now couples `load` → `data.year` → `$effect` → reload.** That's more indirection than the original onMount-only load. It's idiomatic SvelteKit, but it *is* more to follow.
2. **`ExpenseService.getExpenses` now paginates — and that's the one I'd flag.** It fixed a correctness bug, but it changed behavior for **every** caller: the expenses page still loads *all* rows into the browser and filters client-side, so a family with thousands of receipts now holds thousands in memory. Correct, but it moved a latent scaling problem forward. The real fix (someday) is server-side filtering, which I logged.

## The honest part

The **feature** complexity is proportionate. The **churn** was not — the year bug took three tries (onMount → `$page` store → `$app/state` → `load`), and I left worse intermediate states in your running app along the way. The code is now simpler than my middle attempts, but you paid for the detour in review cycles.

Two things I'd call genuine new liabilities, not just size:
- `getExpenses` doing an unbounded client-side load (perf cliff deferred, not removed).
- One more route (`/expenses/import`) and one more service to maintain.

If you want, I can (a) push the expenses/spending filters server-side so `getExpenses` stops loading everything into the browser, or (b) collapse the Spending page's `load`+`effect` coupling if it reads as over-engineered to you. Otherwise, what's there is close to the floor for the feature set you asked for.
